## Purpose

Pages in `apps/dashboard/src/pages/` are the route-level screens of the dashboard: each one fetches one or more backend projections via `@tanstack/react-query`, groups/sorts the rows into sections, and renders them through the shared page primitives. They never talk to the transport directly and never carry ad-hoc inline styling — visual composition is delegated entirely to `@/components/page`. The three exemplars (`Activity.tsx`, `Knowledge.tsx`, `Sessions.tsx`) each open with a substantial header comment explaining the data source, the grouping rule, and any non-obvious design decision (why group by X and not Y), because the grouping logic is usually the one subtle piece of the page.

## Convention

Folder: apps/dashboard/src/pages/** · Extension: .tsx · Files of this role in this subproject: 3

Each page is a single exported function component named after the route (`export function Activity()`, `export function Sessions()`), with private helper functions and small sub-components (row renderers, badges, section headers) declared above it in the same file — no separate helper file for a single page. Grouping/sorting logic lives in a plain typed function near the top (`groupByKind`, `groupSessions`) that takes the raw rows plus whatever formatting deps it needs and returns an array of `{ key, label, items }`-shaped sections; this function is unit-testable in isolation from React. `useQuery` calls use a stable array `queryKey` (e.g. `["sessions", projectsRoot]`) with `enabled: !!projectsRoot` (or `!!activeProject`) so nothing fires before the project is picked. The page always guards the empty/no-project state first (`if (!projectsRoot) return <PageSurface><EmptyState .../></PageSurface>`) before entering the main render path, and the main path itself explicitly branches on `isLoading` / `error` / empty-sections before the populated list.

## How to apply

A new page under `src/pages/` opens with `PageSurface` wrapping an `EditorialBand` (title/subtitle, optionally an `eyebrow`), fetches its data with one or more `useQuery` calls keyed on `projectsRoot`/`activeProject`, computes sections with a plain grouping function memoized via `useMemo`, and renders sections through `DataCard`/`EmptyState`/`SectionHeader` or `CollapsibleGroup` — never raw `<div>` skeletons for structure, only for loading placeholders. Follow the guard: no inline `style={{ color` / `backgroundColor` and no import from `@/components/ds` in this folder; compose from `@/components/page` only.

## Examples

Ref: apps/dashboard/src/pages/Sessions.tsx
```tsx
function categoryLabel(category: string): string {
  const mapped = CATEGORY_LABELS[category];
  if (mapped) return mapped;
  // Unmapped category — capitalise its own value (e.g. "review" → "Review").
  return category.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + category.slice(1);
}

interface SessionSection {
  key: string;
  label: string;
  sessions: SessionRow[];
}
```

Ref: apps/dashboard/src/pages/Activity.tsx
```tsx
export function Activity() {
  const t = useT();
  const projectsRoot = useStore((s) => s.projectsRoot);
  const activeProjectName = useActiveProjectName();

  const { data, isLoading, error } = useQuery<SessionRow[]>({
    queryKey: ["sessions", projectsRoot, SESSION_LIMIT],
    queryFn: () => fetchSessions(projectsRoot!, SESSION_LIMIT),
    enabled: !!projectsRoot,
    staleTime: 30_000,
  });
```
